newsitem.title: EGYPT: Saudi Arabia clears inaugural Palestinian flight.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia clears inaugural Palestinian flight.

text.p: Saudi Arabia has given Palestinian Airlines clearance to make its inaugural flight on Friday morning, the chairman of the airline said on Thursday.
"We have the green light from the Saudi Foreign Ministry at the highest level," chairman Faiz Zaidan told Reuters.

One of the airline's Fokker 50 aircraft will take off from the Egyptian city of Port Said at 7.30 a.m. (0530 GMT) with 48 Gazans bound for Jeddah in Saudi Arabia for the umra or "minor pilgrimage" to the Moslem holy city of Mecca, he added.

The Palestinian Authority has built its own airport in the Gaza Strip but the Israelis will not let Palestinians use it for regular flights. It has received only two flights -- one carrying Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, the other a Moroccan plane bringing aid for the Palestinians, Zaidan said.
A second Fokker 50 will make the trip to Jeddah later on Friday morning and five flights on the same route will follow, spread over Saturday, Sunday and Monday, he said.
The airline, which is wholly owned by the civil aviation authority of the Palestinian Authority, will bring the same pilgrims back between January 21 and 23.
